title: Inverse image of the completed integral twist line, compatibly with coefficient field inclusions
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $h:S'\to S$ a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] let $h^{-1}$ be the inverse image of sheaves along the base-change functor of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]; an $R$-module sheaf $M$ gives the $h^{-1}R$-module sheaf $h^{-1}M$. For a finite extension $H/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_H$, uniformizer $\varpi_H$ and $A_{H,n}=\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^n$, and for $T\in\{S,S'\}$, let $(B)_T$ denote the constant sheaf of a ring $B$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], let $R_{H,T}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{H,T}=\varprojlim_n(A_{H,n})_T$ be the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and, with the roots of unity $\mu_{\ell^r,T}$ and transitions $u\mapsto u^\ell$ [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], inverse limits [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] and tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], let
$$\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T=\varprojlim_r\mu_{\ell^r,T},\qquad \mathcal O_H(1)_T=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T}(\mathcal O_H)_T$$
be the integral twist line of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], an $R_{H,T}$-module by clause 3 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. Let $\gamma_{B}:h^{-1}(B)_S\to(B)_{S'}$ be the comparison of constant ring sheaves of a finite ring $B$ [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] and $c^h_{\mu_{\ell^r}}:h^{-1}\mu_{\ell^r,S}\to\mu_{\ell^r,S'}$ that of roots of unity [def-pur-roots-of-unity-inverse-image]. Then:

1. The ring map $\alpha_{h,H}:h^{-1}R_{H,S}\to R_{H,S'}$ whose composite with the $n$-th projection is $\gamma_{A_{H,n}}\circ h^{-1}(\pi_n)$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings.
2. The map $\tau_h:h^{-1}\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S\to\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_{S'}$ whose composite with the $r$-th projection is $c^h_{\mu_{\ell^r}}\circ h^{-1}(\mathrm{pr}_r)$ is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves.
3. There is an isomorphism $\rho_{h,H}:h^{-1}\mathcal O_H(1)_S\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_H(1)_{S'}$, semilinear over $\alpha_{h,H}$, which on local sections sends $h^{-1}(t\otimes a)$ to $\tau_h(h^{-1}t)\otimes a$ for $a\in\mathcal O_H$.
4. Let $E\subset F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\iota_{EF}:R_{E,T}\to R_{F,T}$ be the ring map whose composite with the projection to $(A_{F,n})_T$ is the projection to $(A_{E,k})_T$ followed by the map induced by $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_F$, for any $k$ with $\varpi_E^k\mathcal O_F\subseteq\varpi_F^n\mathcal O_F$. Let $j_{EF}:\mathcal O_E(1)_T\to\mathcal O_F(1)_T$ be $t\otimes a\mapsto t\otimes a$. Then $\alpha_{h,F}\circ h^{-1}(\iota_{EF})=\iota_{EF}\circ\alpha_{h,E}$ and $\rho_{h,F}\circ h^{-1}(j_{EF})=j_{EF}\circ\rho_{h,E}$.

proof.text: For every $H$, the integral-limit presentation and its pullback compatibility (1) give the ring isomorphism $\alpha_{h,H}$. Its finite coordinates are $\gamma_{A_{H,n}}h^{-1}\pi_n$, the constant comparisons specified in the constant-ring lemma. This proves (1), including transition compatibility.

Apply the compatible-free-tower lemma to the base-change functor $u_h$ of the inverse-image definition (it preserves finite limits and coverings), $R_r=(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_S$, $M_r=\mu_{\ell^r,S}$, $t_r(u)=u^\ell$. $\kappa$ is invertible, as $(\lim\gamma)\kappa=\alpha_{h,\mathbf Q_\ell}$ (Step 1) and $\lim\gamma$ is coordinatewise invertible. Local-freeness (1) gives a pro-etale cover $\widetilde S$ and roots $\zeta_r=\zeta_{r+1}^\ell$; weakly-etale localization (1)-(3) identifies $\widetilde S_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $S_{\mathrm{proet}}/\widetilde S$, on which $(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_S,\mu_{\ell^r,S}$ restrict to $(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_{\widetilde S},\mu_{\ell^r,\widetilde S}$. So $b_r(a)=\zeta_r^a$ are bases with $t_rb_{r+1}(a)=b_r(\bar a)$, and $\theta:h^{-1}\lim M_r\to\lim h^{-1}M_r$ is an isomorphism linear over $\kappa$. The root comparisons $c^h_{\mu_{\ell^r}}$ commute with transitions and are semilinear over $c^h_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}=\gamma_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}$ (root-compatibility lemma (1)-(2), last clause of the constant-ring lemma); they are isomorphisms by the cartesian-twists lemma's first displayed comparison. Hence $\tau_h=(\lim c^h_\mu)\theta$ is an isomorphism with the required (determining) projections, semilinear over $\alpha_{h,\mathbf Q_\ell}$ for the completed action of local-freeness (2). This proves (2).

proof.text: For finite $C$, $\gamma_C$ equals the comparison $\delta_C$ of the constant-module lemma: ring maps out of $h^{-1}C_S$ fixing constant sections agree, $C_S$ being the sheafified constant presheaf and $h^{-1}$ a sheafified colimit. So $\alpha_{h,H},\alpha_{h,\mathbf Q_\ell}$ are the $\alpha_H,\alpha_0$ of the normalized coefficient-tensor lemma; use it with $D=(\mathbf Z_\ell)$, $A=\widehat{\mathbf Z}_\ell$, $B_H=(\mathcal O_H)$, $R_H=\widehat{\mathcal O}_H$. Its $\epsilon$ square makes $\tau_h$ semilinear over $\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$. The action of local-freeness (3) is through the canonical ring map $\widehat{\mathbf Z}_\ell\otimes(\mathcal O_H)\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_H$ given by the structure maps, which is $\beta_H$ by its projection formula. Tensor-presentation transport for $M=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)$ (twist definition), $s=\tau_h$, $a=\alpha_{h,\mathbf Q_\ell}$, $b=\delta_{\mathcal O_H}$, $c=\alpha_{h,H}$ and the $\beta_H$ square gives $\rho_{h,H}$ with the tensor formula and completed semilinearity, proving (3).

source.place: Integral twist: normalized tensor construction and completed action.

proof.text: For $E\subset F$, the coefficient-tensor lemma, with Step 3's identification $\alpha_{h,H}=\alpha_H$, gives the $\iota_{EF}$ square and the compatible constant inclusions. The naturality conclusion of tensor-presentation transport gives the $j_{EF}$ square, with the same $\tau_h$ for both fields. This proves (4).
